source:
Most-viewed: 2000 - 2009
#1 T-mac's 13 points in 33 seconds (Dec 9, 2004 - 27M views)
#2 Kobe scores 81 (Jan 22, 2006 - 22M views)

claim: The five most-viewed moments of the 2000s are McGrady's 13 points in 33 seconds (27,179,256 views), Kobe's 81-point game (21,625,200), Jordan's ball fake (9,377,700), Derek Fisher's 0.4-second game-winner (7,822,632) and Allen Iverson stepping over Tyronn Lue (6,029,208).

source: It has more views than any other NBA moment in our dataset (i.e., it's #1, all-time, at 35M views).
claim: Jordan's last 3 minutes as a Bull is the single most-viewed moment in the dataset, with 34,843,786 aggregated views.

source: Tracy McGrady’s 13 points in 33 seconds is the 2nd most-viewed moment in NBA history, with 27 million views. The 2010s also include the 3rd most-viewed moment: Kobe’s 81 point game
claim: McGrady's 13 points in 33 seconds ranks 2nd across the dataset with 27,179,256 views and Kobe's 81-point game ranks 3rd with 21,625,200, behind Jordan's last 3 minutes as a Bull at 34,843,786.

source: And we're very disappointed to see Reggie's 8 points in 9 seconds outside the top 5 (it's #6).
claim: Reggie Miller's 8 points in 9 seconds is only 6th among 1990s moments, with 5,155,258 views.

source: It's criminal that there's only one Ewing highlight, and it's him on the receiving end of a Jordan dunk
claim: Among the 100 most-viewed 1990s moments exactly one features Patrick Ewing, 'Jordan dunks on Ewing' (1,305,645 views).

source: Unsurprisingly, 3 of the top 5 are Jordan.
claim: Three of the five most-viewed 1980s moments feature Michael Jordan.

source: They pointed to moments such as Ralph Sampson's game-winner (#26) , Tree Bites Man (#31) , or The Sleepy Floyd Game (#42) , not Jordan's first 40-point game (#5) .
claim: Among 1980s moments, Ralph Sampson's game-winner ranks 26th (215,365 views), Tree Bites Man 31st (160,278) and The Sleepy Floyd Game 42nd (102,835).

source: More than half of the plays are Jordan highlights.
claim: 66 of the 100 most-viewed 1990s moments (66%) list Michael Jordan among their players.

source: Stephen Curry has 21 of the top 100 moments from this season.
claim: Stephen Curry appears in 21 of the 100 most-viewed moments of the 2016-17 season.

source: But the #1 moment belongs to Devin Booker’s 70 point game, viewed over 4 million times.
claim: Devin Booker's 70-point game is the most-viewed moment of the 2016-17 season, with 5,107,020 views.

source: Russell Westbrook has #2, when he notched his 42nd triple-double.
claim: Westbrook's record 42nd triple-double is the 2nd most-viewed moment of the 2016-17 season, with 3,913,351 views, behind Booker's 70-point game at 5,107,020.

source: We barely found any videos in our top 100 from pre-Jordan era (‘80 - ‘84).
claim: None of the 100 most-viewed moments in the dataset is dated 1980-1984; all 100 date from 1985 or later.
